Here is the translation:

﴿Has there come to you﴾ [the news of] the Overwhelming (al-Ghashiyah)? [That is,] the Resurrection, because it overwhelms the creatures with its terrors.

Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾. The passage: "﴿وُجُوه يَوْمئِذٍ﴾ عَبَّرَ بِها عَنْ الذَّوات فِي المَوْضِعَيْنِ ﴿خاشِعَة﴾ ذَلِيلَة"

Translation:

﴿Faces, that Day﴾ — he expressed by them the persons (dhawat) in both places. ﴿Humbled﴾ — abased.
﴿Working, toiling﴾: laboring and exhausted, with chains and shackles.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 88, verse 4:

﴿Yaslā﴾ (it shall enter) with the taʾ pronounced with a fatḥah or a ḍammah, "a scorching fire."
﴿They are given to drink from a spring, scalding hot﴾, intensely hot.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 6:

﴿They have no food except from a thorny plant,﴾ it is a kind of thorn that no animal grazes on because of its bitterness.
﴿Some faces that Day will be joyful﴾, radiant (ḥasanah)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 9:

﴿For her striving﴾ in the world through obedience, ﴿well-pleased﴾ in the Hereafter, when she sees its reward.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 88, verse 10:

﴿In a lofty garden﴾, lofty both in its physical place and in its meaning (ḥissan wa-ma‘nan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 11:

﴿Thou shalt not hear﴾ with the ya' and the ta' (i.e., read as both "yasma'" and "tasma'"), ﴿therein any idle talk﴾, i.e., a soul possessing vain speech: babbling of speech.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 12:

﴿Therein is a flowing spring﴾ with water, meaning springs.
﴿In it are raised couches﴾, raised in substance, in rank, and in position.
[Qur'an 88:14] "And cups" — vessels without handles, "placed" (ready) beside the edges of the springs, prepared for their drinking.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 88, verse 15:

﴿And cushions﴾ (wasa'id, pillows) ﴿arranged in rows﴾ (masfufa), one placed beside another, on which one reclines.
[Surah 88, verse 16] ﴿And carpets (zarabi) spread out⁠—﴾ i.e., rugs (busut tanafis) that have a nap (khaml), ﴿spread out﴾, i.e., laid out.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 17:

﴿Will they not then look at the camels, how they were created?﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Makkah should look with the gaze of contemplation (i'tibar) at the camels, how they were created.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 20:

﴿And at the earth, how it is spread out﴾ i.e., it was spread out, so that they may take it as evidence of God Most High's power and His oneness. It (the camel) is mentioned first because they (the Arabs) are more closely connected to it than to other things. His saying "spread out" (sutihat) clearly indicates that the earth is a flat surface (sath), and this is the view of the scholars of the Sharia, not a sphere as the astronomers (ahl al-hay'a) have said, even though this does not contradict a pillar of the Sharia.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 88, verse 21:

﴿So remind﴾ them of Allah's blessings and the proofs of His oneness. "You are only a reminder."

﴿You are not over them a controller.﴾ In another reading (qira'a), with sin (س) instead of sad (ص), so that the word is "musaytir" (one given authority over them). That is, "musallat" (one empowered over them). This was before the command to fight (jihad).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 23:

﴿Illā﴾ (meaning "but" / "however"), ﴿man tawallā﴾ (whoever turns away) from faith, ﴿wa-kafara﴾ (and disbelieves) in the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 24:

﴿So Allah will punish him with the greatest punishment﴾ — the punishment of the Hereafter; and "the lesser" is the punishment of this world, by killing and captivity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, to Us is their return﴾ (their) return (to Us) after death.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 88, verse 26:

﴿Then indeed, upon Us is their reckoning﴾, i.e., their recompense; We shall never leave it (unfulfilled).
